div.div: What galimatron --gal-config-file gal.cfg --log-config-file log.cfg does, for a project that has a Wizard command, a language xslt and a post xslt. Read it top to bottom: the runtime wraps the run, the translator runs fifteen steps one after another, and the panels below open the steps that hide the most.

command line
galimatron --gal-config-file gal.cfg --log-config-file log.cfg

div.div:
rt::translate(args)
runtime_library/translate/detail/translate.cpp
• crash::install(): SEH filter or signals
• log to the console until log.cfg is read
• apply_log_config, then crash::arm_log(): name a crash log beside the log
• read gal.cfg: three passes, paths made absolute
• set the path report (committed-report)
• outer leaf_spy::try_catch: prints and logs every error

div.div:
translate_by_config
translate/detail/translate_by_config.cpp
• filesystem_decorator_t with places: the .gal place(s), the intermediate place, one place per other-files store (panel I)
• summary builder and a scope guard that always writes galimatron_summary.xml
• process_result: routes the output of every step to a place

div.div:
start of the run
• fsd.do_jobs_at_begin(): create folders, delete the files of places marked at_begin (the intermediate folder; the output .gal in
separate mode)
• crash::arm_summary()
• add six directory xsl:params to every enabled user transform
• read the .gal files lazily from the input place, read gal.version

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 950px; height: 1px; padding-top: 237px; margin-left: 4086px;

div.div:
translator::translate(config)
translator/detail/translate.cpp
• prepare_transforms(): builds the list of steps (panel A)
• one Taskflow task per step, chained with precede: strictly one after another
• one static tf::Executor for the process (Saxon attaches a Graal thread to each worker)
• executor().run(taskflow).get()

div.div:
• one ANTLR parse per .gal file, one chunk
vertex per file
• listener_t walks the tree, builder_t adds
vertices and registers them in the holder
• keeps source text and comments on the
vertices
• skipped when language_state_ is already
set

div.div:
• a Taskflow subflow of twelve checks:
shape of versions, anchors, hashes (panel
B)
• then compile_for_validation =
cpp2post_cpp::translate
• checks the file as it is. The Wizard
command is checked later, by the Wizard
step
• prints lang-parsed.xml

div.div:
• exactly one statement:
is_wizard_command_single
• apply_one(type) or the batch loop with
refresh_checks() (panel C)
• each command calls
may_execute_wizard_command() first
• at the end the command text becomes //
lines at the top of its chunk

div.div:
the run failed
• the exception is a LEAF exception; on a worker it became a captured_leaf_exception
• the inner try_catch copies its text into the summary <error>
• do_jobs_at_end does not run: delayed .gal are dropped, stale files stay
• the outer try_catch logs the text; the exit code is 1

div.div: The list of steps is built, not written. You configure the interesting steps (the seed). transform_sequence_builder inserts the conversions between them, so that each step gets the representation it needs.

div.div:
the seed: what is configured
• cpp2cpp_validate
• cpp2cpp_wizard
• only with a language xslt: cpp2cpp_before_xslt, your language xslts
(xml2xml, in config order), cpp2cpp_after_xslt
• your post xslts (xml2xml)
They keep their order. A step with "enable": false is not in the seed.

div.div:
the catalog: state transforms, one edge each (domain, state type)
• gal2cpp LANGUAGE GaL → CPP
• cpp2gal LANGUAGE CPP → GaL
• cpp2xml LANGUAGE CPP → XML
• xml2saxon LANGUAGE XML → SAXON
• xml2cpp LANGUAGE SAXON → CPP
• cpp2post_cpp LANGUAGE CPP → POST CPP
• post_cpp2post_xml POST CPP → POST XML
• post_xml2saxon POST XML → POST SAXON

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1040px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1675px; margin-left: 1406px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #222222;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#222222, #d0d0d0); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
builder_t::complete_transform_sequence (translator/detail/transform_sequence_builder.cpp, unit-tested)
1. check_transform_sequence: LANGUAGE steps first, then POST_LANGUAGE steps. A return to LANGUAGE is an error
2. check_state_transforms: the catalog must hold the seven edges a run needs
3. before each seed step, ensure_state: a breadth-first search over the catalog finds the shortest path from the current representation (the language part
may not leave LANGUAGE)
4. when the language part is done: append cpp2gal, unless the last step already is one
5. no post xslt: continue to POST XML. A post xslt needs SAXON, so the path ends in post_xml2saxon

div.div: The seed steps are in the Taskflow chain as they are. The Wizard step is skipped at run time when no Wizard statement exists. Tests use prepare_testing_transforms() instead: the seed is only the steps that a testing_t flag switches on, and the builder inserts a conversion only where two seed steps do not meet.

div.div: cpp2cpp_validate_t::build() puts twelve checks in a Taskflow subflow. They run on worker threads. An arrow means "runs after". The edges are those of intermediate/taskflow.dot.

div.div:
• Seven checks (the four root checks, is anonymous versions owned, both hash checks) do nothing when the Wizard command is, or contains, create root aggregate: the root does not exist yet.
• A hash of a version named by create hash … force or delete hash … force is not checked in this run.
• A failure is thrown on a worker: fail(code, what, where) runs augment_where inside capture_or_rethrow, and subflow.join() rethrows on the caller.
• Which error is reported first is not deterministic when several checks fail.
• validate_memo_t caches only the three root gate checks (shared mutex, success only). It is replaced together with the checker (refresh_checks).
• Wizard commands are not in this graph. The Wizard step calls may_execute_wizard_command() itself (panel C).

before each change.

div.div:
batch (apply_wizard_batch)
• may_execute_wizard_command(): batch context is a chunk
• for each item: refresh_checks() (new memo, new checker, re-snapshot of aggregates)
• overwrite the stored statement: type, data = the item
• is_wizard_batch_command_create()
• apply_one(item.type)
• restore the statement

div.div:
closed versions
closed = a root version at or before the last hashed declaration (last_hashed).
The protection is entirely in the validator (wizard-closed-version rules). The apply_*
functions assume it passed, and after any change of hashes or declarations they must
refresh last_hashed, or the next command of a batch sees a stale seal.

div.div:
1 register the label callback; root aggregate first
create_merged_versions_entities (merge.cpp): for each root version, first the parked bodies (version before N) it owns,
then its own statements. delete; is skipped.

div.div:
2 compile_merged_versions_entities (compile_merged.cpp), once per aggregate
a. naming_unnamed_tags: a tag without a name takes it from a tag-name-from label (must match identifier_pattern)
b. remember_values_before: the value just before each statement, for the history
c. per version: check_labels_in_version → compile_tags_in_version → template_engine::render → write tag_container
d. root only: compile_orderings_in_version

div.div:
3 each other aggregate, in file order
the same two calls. The root's statements of each version are copied in first, so an aggregate can override them. Not
copied: a root tag with mode local; nothing at all when the aggregate's version mode is local or own. A deleted version
has no body.

div.div:
4 notify_default_aggregates_ordering
ranks_of_ordering: a directed graph from the {A, B, C} chains, topological sort, rank = longest chain of predecessors, and
a check that the result is a strict weak order. Unnamed aggregates follow, in file order. The stored index is the final
position.

every label reference becomes its static value. The compiled part keeps no label references.

div.div:
last declaration wins: compile_tags_in_version walks the statements from the end; the first one seen per resolved name is kept, and a delete name; consumes
the name. Deleting a label is an error. Deleting an absent tag only logs a warning.
templates: template_engine::render builds JSON from the version's tags (several values → an array, {{name}} means {{name.0}}) and renders each _te string
with inja. The result is stored per (version, string); the language graph keeps the raw text.
errors: throw_compiler(text) = LEAF cpp2post_cpp + e_what_info, with path (through report_path), aggregate and version attached.

div.div:
a small example
language: root version 0 { currency = { "EUR" }; }, Apple version 0 { price = { "3" }; }, Apple version 1 { price = { "4" }; }
compiled Apple, version 0: currency = EUR, price = 3
compiled Apple, version 1: currency = EUR (from the root, copied in), price = 4 (the last declaration wins)
Version 1 of Apple never repeated the currency: the compiled XML says it for every version.

div.div:
<chunk><location><filesystem path root relative …/></location> per file
<root-aggregate name> / <aggregate name index> with …-version-declarations (index status comment hash) and …-version-definitions (index or owner, mode)
<tag index name mode layout-mark> with <label-refs><static><label-ref name index/>, <values><value index><string delimiter template-engine>, records, arrays
<label index name> with <static><values>…<tag-name-from/> or <dynamic value/>
<ordering index name>, <delete index name?/>
Wizard marks: <dynamic wizard="new-version|new-aggregate|new-root-aggregate"/>, and <dynamic labelname="value"/> on a copied tag that uses a dynamic label
<string-delimiters>, and <history> beside <language>

div.div:
the same skeleton, but each version lists only the effective tags of the compiled state, in order
a tag always has its name (resolved from tag-name-from)
no label statements, no label-refs: each static label becomes an attribute on <value>, <value index="0" field="type">
<string> holds the rendered text and no template-engine mark
<orderings><ordering name index="position"/></orderings> under each aggregate version definition
no Wizard marks
<history>: per version, per aggregate, the changes (add, replace, delete, label, ordering, create-aggregate, delete-version)

div.div:
the decorator's printout (filesystem_decorator.cpp): split the old path by the owning place → merge with the new parts (the place root wins) → write.once and already saved? error → mark the file as rewritten (so the end-of-run cleanup keeps it) → if_content_differ: compare with cache or disk → write now, or set pending_write for do_jobs_at_end.
It returns finally_path. process_result turns those paths into the summary entry (relative to gal.cfg with committed-report).

A SaxonApiException is turned into text first (printout_native_saxon_exception), then thrown as LEAF translator.

div.div: Errors are Boost.LEAF exceptions with a domain, a subdomain and payloads. Thrown inside galimatron, caught in the runtime, printed once.

div.div:
throw: leaf::throw_exception(domain, subdomain, e_what_info, [code], …)
context by RAII guards: augment_domain, augment_path, augment_aggregate, augment_version, augment_where (keep the returned
object alive)
types only in common_library/exception_declaration.hpp

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.div:
on the main thread the exception travels to the nearest try_catch.
on a Taskflow worker there is no LEAF context: capture_or_rethrow runs the code under leaf::try_capture_all and throws
captured_leaf_exception. subflow.join() or future.get() rethrows it on the caller's thread, and leaf_spy unloads the payloads
there.

div.div:
inner catch: translate_by_config → runtime::try_catch, is_throw_out = true. leaf_spy::spy_handler_t loads every domain,
subdomain, enum and payload, prints Exception details: into a stream; notify_printed copies the text into the summary
<error>; the exception goes on.

div.div:
outer catch: translate_impl_t::translate → the same wrapper; the text is logged with fLogmeE; the result is 1. is_testing_mode
lets the exception leave translate() in tests, which print it with print_leaf_exception.

div.div:
Not LEAF: syntax errors are antlr4::ParseCancellationException (the spy prints them with a dynamic_cast); a bad log config or a failed merge_paths is std::runtime_error. Both show "NO DOMAIN-SPECIFIC EXCEPTION CATEGORY MATCHED" in the printout.
The path in the printed text is spelled from copies in e_path_info (committed_report, config_dir), because the run's path report may be gone when the text is built.

div.div:
• "once": writing the same path twice in one run is an error.
• Roots of places may not be nested (checked in add_place).
• "at the end" runs in do_jobs_at_end, only after a run that succeeded.
• The log folder is opened by Logme from log.cfg. It is not a place.
• Nothing checks that a relative .. path stays in its place, so confinement is by construction.
